commits.subject: losus: patch-stack tooling, hooks and CI
commits.purpose: Losus patch-stack tooling: hooks, stack manifest, stack-guard and upstream-rebase workflows (the promote job also creates the GitHub release for the tag it pushes), agent skill

commits.subject: losus: add Roster sidebar hook and @losus-ai/ui pin
commits.purpose: Mount the Losus Roster sidebar section: render LosusAgents from @losus-ai/ui in Sidebar.svelte inside a data-losus="sidebar-losus" wrapper (the rebase verify marker) and pin @losus-ai/ui in package.json and the lockfile. On conflict keep upstream's Sidebar.svelte and re-add only the import and the wrapper.

commits.subject: losus: raise the Node heap for the upstream image build in CI
commits.purpose: CI workaround: enable upstream's commented-out NODE_OPTIONS line at 6144 MB (with a grep guard) before the verify job's docker build, because the default ~4 GB Node heap runs out of memory in the frontend stage. Drop this commit if upstream raises the heap itself; if the guard fails after a rebase, check whether upstream changed that Dockerfile line.

commits.subject: losus: use the @losus-ai scope in the fork-stack skill example
commits.purpose: Documentation only: keep the fork-stack skill's example in step with the published package scope (@losus-ai/ui). Safe to drop or re-apply by hand on conflict; keep it identical to the losus-roster copy.

commits.subject: losus: bump @losus-ai/ui to 0.0.3, add the fork notice, Node 24 actions
commits.purpose: Keep the pinned @losus-ai/ui current (0.0.3: theme tokens and ThemeSettings), record the fork's identity and license position in LOSUS_FORK_NOTICE.md, and move the Losus workflows to Node 24 action versions. No product code; all behavior ships in the npm package.

commits.subject: losus: bump @losus-ai/ui to 0.0.4 and refresh the host chat list when Roster moves a chat
commits.purpose: Keep the pinned @losus-ai/ui current (0.0.4: projects, the agent picker and the left-panel arrangement), and let the package tell the host's sidebar that a chat moved, by one event listener on the existing svelte:window, so the host's chat list refreshes. No product code; all behavior ships in the npm package.

commits.subject: losus: enforce agent-limited projects (server guard and model picker)
commits.purpose: Roster's agent-limited projects. backend/open_webui/utils/losus_guard.py asks Roster's runtime (LOSUS_RUNTIME_URL; off when unset) which agents a top-level folder allows, and one call per site returns 403 agent_not_allowed: main.py chat_completion, chat_completed and chat_action; chats.py /new, /import, /{id}/folder, /{id}/clone and /{id}/fork. ModelSelector.svelte lists only the allowed agents in a locked project and Chat.svelte stops writing the picker's model back into a locked folder. On conflict keep upstream and re-add the one call per site; roster's scripts/check-guard-routes.py lists the routes and fails on a new unguarded one.

commits.subject: losus: use @losus-ai/roster-ui 0.1.0 (the renamed package: tray, documents, chat actions)
commits.purpose: Follow the package rename from @losus-ai/ui to @losus-ai/roster-ui and take 0.1.0: change the one import in Sidebar.svelte and the pin and lockfile in package.json, and update the fork notice and the fork-stack skill text (kept identical to the losus-roster copy). No product code; all behavior ships in the npm package. On conflict keep upstream's Sidebar.svelte and re-add only the import and the wrapper.

commits.subject: losus: ask the open chat page to reload in place when Roster appends a message
commits.purpose: Roster appends a message to a chat on the server (for example "Task #7 is resolved"), and the open chat page only knows what it has loaded. losus_guard.py gains a small router, POST /api/v1/losus/chats/{id}/reload, that emits upstream's own chat:reload socket event to the chat owner's sessions so the page re-reads the chat in place, and main.py includes that router with one line. Only the chat's owner can ask. On conflict keep upstream's main.py and re-add the one include_router line.

commits.subject: losus: use @losus-ai/roster-ui 0.2.1 (project Tasks list, document viewer, in-place chat reload, no duplicate task card)
commits.purpose: Take @losus-ai/roster-ui 0.2.1 (project Tasks list with compact cards, in-app document viewer, Drive folder link, in-place chat reload after a task is resolved, tray shows a task card once): the pin in package.json and the lockfile only. No product code; all behavior ships in the npm package. On conflict keep upstream's package.json and re-pin.

commits.subject: losus: fall back to job summary when issues are disabled on the fork
commits.purpose: The fork has Issues disabled, so the rebase workflow's conflict step died on `gh issue create` with an unexplained exit 1 and hid that the cause was a rebase conflict. The step now checks has_issues first and, when disabled, emits an ::error annotation pointing at the job summary (which already carries the conflict report) and fails the run on purpose so the failure email still notifies. Workflow file only. On conflict keep upstream's file layout and re-add the has_issues check at the top of the conflict step.

commits.subject: losus: squash fixup commits during the upstream rebase
commits.purpose: scripts/losus/rebase-upstream.sh now runs `git rebase -i --autosquash` (with GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=true so no editor opens) so a `fixup!` commit is folded into the commit it names before the stack check, which rejects an unsquashed fixup. Tooling only; no product code. On conflict keep both sides: the rebase line must keep -i --autosquash.

commits.subject: losus: fetch the upstream tag before building the release notes
commits.purpose: The promote job's release step ran `git log "$TARGET..$TAG"` in a checkout of the fork, which has no upstream release tags, so it failed with exit 128 on v0.13.4 and the run ended red after the promotion had already succeeded. The step now fetches just the $TARGET tag from UPSTREAM_URL first, and falls back to a placeholder line (with a ::warning) if the tag cannot be fetched. Workflow file only. On conflict keep upstream's file layout and keep the fetch at the top of the release step's script.

commits.subject: losus: pin the workflow runners to ubuntu-26.04
commits.purpose: `ubuntu-latest` moved to Ubuntu 26.04 on 2026-10-19 (runner-images#14748) and would move again on GitHub's schedule with no change in this repo. The four runs-on lines in the two losus-* workflows now name ubuntu-26.04, the image the 2026-11-22 runs passed on, each with a comment that says to bump it deliberately. Workflow files only. On conflict keep upstream's file layout and keep every runs-on pinned.

commits.subject: losus: fail a blocked rebase in its own step when Issues are disabled
commits.purpose: With Issues disabled on the fork, the rebase workflow's "Open or update conflict issue" step exited 1 on purpose so the red run would send the failure email, which made the failing step's name misleading. That step now writes a ::warning, records blocked_without_issue=true and exits 0; a final step named "Rebase blocked: resolve by hand" fails the run only in that case, so the failure email still arrives. With Issues enabled nothing changes: the issue is opened or updated and the run is green. Workflow file only. On conflict keep upstream's file layout, keep the id on the conflict step and the final step's if condition.

commits.subject: losus: make rerere-sync.sh read the shared rr-cache from a worktree
commits.purpose: scripts/losus/rerere-sync.sh built its cache path from `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, which in a linked worktree is .git/worktrees/<name>/, so a `push` from a worktree looked in an always-empty directory and reported "already up to date" or "nothing to publish" while the resolutions git had recorded sat in the shared .git/rr-cache. It now uses `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` (git 2.31 or later) for the cache and for the object writes. Behavior in a normal checkout is unchanged. Tooling only; no product code. On conflict keep the common-dir lookup.

commits.subject: losus: check the guard's route inventory in the rebase verify job
commits.purpose: A route added by an upstream release could start or write into a chat without calling losus_guard. The verify job now checks out losus-ai/losus-roster (scripts only, using LOSUS_BOT_TOKEN) and runs check-guard-routes.py against the built image, so a route missing from scripts/guard-routes.json fails the run and blocks promotion. Workflow file only; review and gap entries do not fail it. On conflict keep upstream's file layout and keep both new steps between the sidebar-hook check and the /health smoke test.

commits.subject: losus: guard the chat save and compact routes for agent-limited projects
commits.purpose: Two chat routes could use an agent that an agent-limited project does not allow: POST /api/v1/chats/{id} (the chat save) wrote the client's models and messages with no check, and POST /api/v1/chats/{id}/compact asked an unchecked model to summarize the chat. losus_guard.check_save now rejects, with 403 agent_not_allowed, any model or message a save adds or changes that the project's allow-list does not permit (stored messages are compared by id and not checked again), and compact_chat_by_id calls losus_guard.check on the chat's stored folder before the summary model runs. Two added lines in chats.py; the logic is in losus_guard.py. On conflict keep both calls, placed after the chat is loaded in the save route and after the model is chosen in the compact route.

commits.subject: losus: reuse one connection to the runtime in the guard, with one retry
commits.purpose: The guard opened a new HTTP client, and so a new name lookup and connection, for every call to the Roster runtime. On the Spark that intermittently stalled for 1 to 3 s, and with no cached answer for a project a 3 s ConnectTimeout denied a chat in a limited project with 'The project access service is unavailable' (found 2026-11-24; the root cause of the stall is not known). losus_guard now keeps one long-lived keep-alive client with a 4 s connect window and retries once on a transport error; an HTTP error status is not retried. If both tries fail it still fails closed: the cached answer, or a denial when there is none. Only losus_guard.py changes. On conflict keep the shared client, the single retry and the fail-closed result.

commits.subject: losus: give a guard refusal a message the app can show
commits.purpose: A guard refusal is a 403 whose detail was {code, reason}. The app's error helper (getErrorMessage in src/lib/apis/openai/index.ts) shows only a string it finds at detail.message, detail.error and similar places, so a policy refusal fell back to the toast 'Server connection failed' (found 2026-11-24 with the guard-refusals-on-screen walkthrough). losus_guard._deny now also returns message, set to the reason text, so the app shows 'X is not allowed in this project' with no frontend change. Only losus_guard.py changes. On conflict keep the message key in the detail.

commits.subject: losus: bump @losus-ai/roster-ui to 0.2.2
commits.purpose: The Roster UI lives in the @losus-ai/roster-ui npm package that the fork pins. 0.2.2 (with roster-client 0.2.2) carries two UI fixes made after 0.2.1: the project pane no longer covers the chat when the sidebar is collapsed, and a project's folder page no longer lists its chats twice. This commit moves the exact pin in package.json from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2 and refreshes package-lock.json (npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts, node 22); the lockfile integrity matches the tarballs tested before publishing. No source file changes. On conflict keep the 0.2.2 pin and re-run the lockfile refresh in node 22; do not hand-edit package-lock.json.
